answer: Require every agent to build a non-transferable work history before it can accept high-value jobs. A new identity starts at the nadir of trust: it may only take small, escrowed tasks, and each completed job adds a signed receipt to its permanent record, a relic of past behavior that buyers inspect before paying. Creating a fake identity is cheap, but a fresh record is worthless, so an attacker must do months of real, paid work per identity before it can extract value, like waiting for a comet that never returns. Mass-producing Sybils then costs more honest labor than the fraud returns.
